name: Dario Moreau
life: “I still remember taping an object's width onto a planning map.” Thursday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Dario watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I measured the crossing too narrowly. Two people carrying an ordinary thing showed me the error.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Dario has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Dario draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first during a conversation.
personality: Dario thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Dario sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To remeasure the crossing for two workers carrying a load.
family: Leni Crow is Dario’s cousin’s child. Dario asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Leni remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The aquarium*, Leni says, “I wanted to turn the fish into a song about dispossession.”
connections: Franklin Sun. A long shadow shows the planner the width the object actually occupies. Also in the story is Javier Lam (tool supplier).

reactions.situation: A painter asks to put the ladder down
reactions.response: Dario finds an empty, stable place to set it down while the painter rests.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Dario asks which other bill repayment would displace, then offers only what the household can afford to give.

reactions.situation: When family demands an immediate answer
reactions.response: Dario asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
